newsitem.title: MEXICO: FEMSA Q1 results slightly disappointing.
newsitem.headline: FEMSA Q1 results slightly disappointing.

text.p: Mexican brewer and bottler Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (FEMSA) reported first-quarter results mostly in line with market expectations but with a few minor disappointments, analysts said on Tuesday.

Analyst were most concerned over flat beer sales volumes for Mexico's No. 2 beer-maker and negative volume growth for the Argentine side of Coca-Cola FEMSA, the subsidiary also known as KOF that bottles and distributes soft drinks in Mexico and Argentina.
Otherwise, those two main divisions performed well while the packaging division and Oxxo convenience store chain turned in solid quarters, they said.

FEMSA's main first-quarter numbers came in below those predicted in a Reuters survey of three analysts. Net profit was 293.48 million pesos versus the survey's predicted 397 million pesos, operating income was 484.72 million peosos against the predicted 573 million pesos, and gross profit was 2.11 billion pesos as opposed to the forecast 2.481 billion pesos.
But significantly higher expectations from one of the surveyed analysts may have skewed the survey somewhat.

Perhaps the most glaring weakness in the FEMSA report was a sales volumes decline of 1.4 percent for KOF in Argentina. That figure does not take into account the San Isidro area concession rights, which KOF acquired in February 1996. Including San Isidro, volumes grew 1.3 percent.
"It wasn't the 10 percent growth that they were having the past couple of quarters," Will Landers, a food and beverage analyst with Lehman Brothers, told Reuters.
In response, KOF ADRs took a beating on Monday, closing 2-3/4 lower to 33-1/2, although it began to rebound on Tuesday, picking up 1-3/4 to 34-7/8 in morning trade.
In the beer division, for weeks the company was telling analysts that sales volumes would be flat.

"Well, they were," analyst Francisco Rivero of Valores Finamex in New York told Reuters after the Q1 earnings report. "They just had an aggressive price increase (22 percent in March) and obviously that brought down the volume trend in the first quarter. Even though, I expected something better."

FEMSA sold 4.954 million hectoliters of beer in the first quarter, a slight increase from 4.927 million hectoliters in Q1 1996. The Reuters survey predicted beers sales volume of 4.85 million hectoliters.
The bright side was that beer exports to the United States rose by 19.6 percent, led by the Dos Equis brands.
In addition, a FEMSA press release played up an increase of 171.5 percent in beer operating income and volume growth of 14 percent in KOF's Mexican operations.
Operating results on the beer side were helped by the price increase and lower costs for grains and packaging, the company and analysts said.

"Dos Equis is performing very well, which is interesting because everybody's been talking about Sol," said Scott Wilkins of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City, referring to FEMSA's showcase brand, Sol, which has fueled most of the export growth in recent quarters.
But overall exports were basically flat, growing to 251,000 hectoliters from 248,000 a year ago.

"They're still struggling in South America with exports," Francisco Chavez, an analyst with Smith Barney in New York, told Reuters. "That doens't look like its going to get better any time soon, so they're falling behind Modelo."
Grupo Modelo SA de CV is Mexico's No. 1 brewer.
